title: Can an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Pipeline Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that measured whether inserting an executable emulator validator (and a single-step repair policy) into a generate–validate–repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). The study used a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine). A single shared initial candidate per task was produced by gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated by both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) performed full intent-constraint and workflow-policy checks and allowed ≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode. Outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We present artifact-grounded methodological detail, representative validator diagnostics, deterministic reconciliation accounting, and a focused discussion of why the shared-generation paired design produced a statistical ceiling and how future confirmatory designs can better exercise verification/repair subsystems.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored to convert operator intent into concrete network configuration commands. While LLMs can produce syntactically valid commands, text-level plausibility does not guarantee safe enactment: configuration sequences must satisfy workflow invariants (for example, shutdown→change→restore ordering, make-before-break uplink switchover, or group-availability constraints). Prior work therefore proposes integrating verification, emulation, or veto layers so generated candidates are validated before application. Evaluating these guarded pipelines requires closed-loop executable tests that detect semantic violations not visible from textual checks.

We designed a preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) to isolate whether an executable emulator validator (plus a bounded repair policy) reduces semantic failures when the identical generator output is presented to both (a) a baseline LLM-only suggestion workflow and (b) a guarded generate–validate–repair workflow. Using a shared-initial-candidate paired design intentionally holds generator output constant across the pair so the analysis isolates the marginal effect of validation and repair on identical LLM outputs. This mechanistic focus differs from prior corpus- or model-comparison studies that conflate generator variability with validator effects.

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-rich paired experiment (N=120 pairs) fixing the generator and measuring the incremental effect of an executable validator and bounded repair; (2) exact execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation that document completed preregistered protocol items (planned vs completed episodes, model-call accounting, contamination checks, and validator/scorer traces); (3) artifact-grounded diagnostics and interpretation of a ceiling outcome (100% success in both conditions) with exact McNemar and bootstrap reporting; and (4) concrete, evidence-grounded methodological recommendations for future confirmatory designs that aim to exercise repair behavior.
sections.related_work: Two research strands most closely frame this study. First, executable-benchmark and network-verification work demonstrates that closed-loop emulation reveals semantic failure modes—sequencing errors, make-before-break mistakes, and group-availability violations—that textual or syntactic checks miss (see NetConfArena and executable-benchmark studies). Second, a growing literature on tool-augmented LLM agents advocates generate–validate–repair loops and bounded-autonomy guardrails (veto layers, canaries, translation-to-formal-model) to reduce operational risk. Benchmarks and prototype tool papers report that validator/repair components can detect regressions and prevent unsafe enactments, but systematic, closed-loop comparisons under identical harnesses and controlled generator variance remain limited. Our experimental lens complements those works by fixing generator outputs and asking: given an identical generated candidate, does an executable validator plus one-step repair change the final semantic outcome?
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study preregistration (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) fixed a paired-binary confirmatory design with exactly N=120 intent→configuration tasks partitioned deterministically into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine; 40 tasks each). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The prespecified primary test was the exact two-sided McNemar; complementary reporting included a bootstrap-percentile 95% confidence interval with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729. The preregistration specified exclusion/contamination rules, a repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), deterministic emulator resets, and the shared-generation paired stage to isolate validator/repair effects.

Task generation and structured payloads. Tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest entry includes initial_state, expected_final_state, intent (natural-language), required_sequence (canonical ordered actions the validator enforces), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level). The explicit required_sequence enables structured checking of sequencing and workflow policies rather than heuristic text matching.

Generation and model configuration. The declared model for shared initial candidate production was gpt-5-mini; execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and model_calls_used = 120. The execution contract used a single shared_initial_generation stage (stage_counts recorded as shared_initial_generation = 120) so each pair used the identical generated candidate. The shared-generation choice increases internal validity for measuring validator/repair marginal effects but reduces opportunities for the repair policy to be exercised when the generator already produces correct candidates for the curated task bank.

Validator semantics and repair policy. The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0), an executable emulator/validator that enforces task-encoded policy fields such as must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, and make-before-break patterns. The validator executes candidates in an emulated final-state checker and emits structured traces: validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy triggered a single repair prompt only when validator.violation_count>0; repair artifacts (repair_prompt_trace, repair_provider_trace) were to be archived if generated. In this run validator.violation_count = 0 for all guarded episodes and therefore repair_applied = false for all pairs.

Instrumentation, contamination controls, and deterministic reconciliation. The harness enforced deterministic container/image resets between tasks (container checksum + deterministic seeds) and recorded provider-call audits (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120 completed; cache_miss_count = 120; cross-condition cache reuse = false). Contamination heuristics (duplicate-output detection and cross-condition cache-key reuse) were applied; none triggered exclusions. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, complete_pair_count = 120, and consistent provider/audit accounting. All instrumentation logs and scoring traces are archived as execution and analysis artifacts.

Statistical procedures and degeneracy handling. The prespecified primary test was exact two-sided McNemar on paired semantic-success labels. Complementary uncertainty reporting used a paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). When empirical contingency tables contain zero discordant pairs, bootstrap resamples reproduce the identical paired table and the paired-difference distribution is degenerate: every resample yields 0.00, producing a zero-width bootstrap interval. We explicitly predefined this bootstrap procedure in the preregistration and report the exact bootstrap parameters to make the degeneracy interpretable.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcome. The run completed per the preregistered stopping rule: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition-level counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) report baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0, guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table is n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. These numeric results are reproduced in analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Per-topology breakdown. Tasks were deterministically partitioned into 40 tasks per topology class. Per-topology outcomes recorded in the archived manifests are:
- Edge (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
- Core (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
- Leaf–spine (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
Table 1 (captioned) summarizes these counts and success rates by topology class and is fully consistent with the task manifest entries and scoring JSON artifacts.

Representative validator diagnostics and task-level examples. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json and task-000002/task-000003 examples) show normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer; parsed_command_count equals required_command_count from the task payload; validation_after.valid = true; repair_applied = false; validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; validator_version = 5.0. For example, task-000001 required_sequence = [shutdown edge1, set MTU, set VLAN, restore edge1] and the shared generated candidate executed that sequence exactly; the validator's trace recorded observed_touched_field_count = 3, parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, violation_count = 0. Similar traces are present for task-000002 and task-000003 (make-before-break uplink switchover; paired-link atomic MTU change). Representative response files and JSON scorings are archived and checksummed in the execution manifest.

Repair incidence and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count = 0 in every guarded episode, repair_applied = false across the run and no repair_provider_trace artifacts were generated. Consequently, preregistered secondary endpoints that quantify repair incidence, repair-call counts, or repair-induced convergence are vacuous for this run and are reported as such in analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv and the repair fields in execution scoring JSONs). The absence of repair activity is an empirical finding grounded in the archived validator traces rather than an execution omission.

Contamination, missingness, and reconciliation. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty and analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 with zero technical or instrumentation exclusions. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms provider-audit consistency (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120, cross-condition cache reuse = false) and pair accounting (n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0). No post-preregistration deviations were recorded.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the ceiling outcome. The preregistered shared-generation paired design specifically isolates the marginal effect of validation/repair on fixed generator outputs. In the archived synthetic task bank and under the frozen generator prompt strategy, the shared initial candidates satisfied the deterministic emulator validator in all 120 tasks; as a result the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to exercise repair behavior and could not reduce semantic failures relative to the baseline. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 and degenerate bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00] mathematically reflect this full concordance.

Design trade-offs and implications for confirmatory inference. The shared-generation design reduces generator variance and increases internal precision for estimating validator effects on identical outputs, but it also reduces the operational realism where generator outputs vary. For trials intended to demonstrate repair utility under realistic generator error rates we recommend one or more of the following (each of which is directly supported by metadata fields in the archived manifests): (a) independent generation per condition so the validator can intercept generator errors that arise under prompt/model variability; (b) controlled prompt perturbations (the preregistration's exploratory perturbation axes can be enabled to raise generator error incidence); or (c) stratified selection of tasks with high difficulty metadata (dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) to increase the chance of generator-produced violations. The study's archived difficulty metadata and representative traces provide concrete metadata needed to operationalize such stratified designs.

Operational value of deterministic validator traces. Even in a run where no repairs were applied, deterministic validator traces (which rules were checked, touched-field counts, and explicit valid/invalid flags) contribute operator-facing auditability and post-hoc analysis. The archived artifacts demonstrate end-to-end instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, scoring traces, deterministic reconciliation) that can be used for operator explanations, compliance reporting, and third-party audits in deployment contexts where generators sometimes err.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: strong—deterministic provisioning, explicit provider-audit logs, zero exclusions, and complete pair accounting. Construct validity: limited by the fact that the validator enforces a specific set of policy encodings derived from synthetic task payloads; some production failure modes (vendor-specific timing, partial observability, real-world telemetry delays) may not be modeled. External validity: constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈0.40 (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15); with observed baseline = 0.00 those assumptions do not hold and the primary test is uninformative for demonstrating the originally targeted effect size.

Guidance for future confirmatory runs. Based on the archived manifest and traces we recommend: (1) enable independent generation per condition or introduce controlled prompt perturbations to ensure the guarded pipeline is exercised; (2) allow multi-iteration repairs with archival of repair traces to analyze repair convergence; (3) evaluate multiple generator families under the same executable harness to measure cross-model generality; (4) extend emulator fidelity toward multi-vendor behavior and partial observability; and (5) prioritize construction or partnership to acquire production-rooted incident corpora with verifiable ground truth. The stored difficulty metadata (dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) can be used to select tasks with higher expected generator failure rates for targeted follow-up experiments.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120 pairs) comparing an executable generate–validate–repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow while holding generator output fixed. All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0); bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The result documents a ceiling on the curated synthetic task bank and clarifies that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear under generator variance. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we demonstrate how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing. The archived artifacts support follow-up studies that relax shared-generation, enable independent generation per condition, expand repair budgets, and compare generator families to quantify repair utility under realistic generator variance and production heterogeneity.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
